learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge of analytic geometry of Euclidean plane and space.
Ability to apply some abstract notions through the geometric interpretation of linear algebra problems and the translation into algebraic terms of some geometric problems.
Ability to choose geometric and/or algebraic tools to solve concrete problems.
Ability to correctly and clearly express problems and results.
Ability to develop and deepen unknown or partially known topics.

syllabus_topics: Vector spaces: algebraic structures (groups and fields), definitions, models and fundamental properties.
Intersection subspace, span of a finite set of vectors and sum subspace.
Determinant of a square matrix and its properties.
Definition and properties of the rank of a matrix.
Definition and properties of a linear application.
Kernel and image of a linear application.
Matrices associated with linear applications between finite-dimensional vector spaces.
Scalar, vector and mixed products between free vectors and their properties.
Parametric and Cartesian representations of a line.
Reciprocal positions of two lines; pencils of lines.
Angles and distances in a real Euclidean plane.
Parametric and Cartesian representations of a line and a plane in real Euclidean space.
Reciprocal positions between lines; reciprocal positions between lines and planes; pencils of planes.
Angles and distances in Euclidean space.
assessment_rules: The assessment is based on a 2-hour written exam including 4 numerical exercises and 2 theoretical questions. To pass, at least 3 'a' points of the numerical exercises must be correct, at least two of the four numerical exercises must be completed (including the Analytic Geometry exercise), and sufficient mastery of definitions for theoretical questions must be demonstrated. The final grade, expressed out of thirty, reflects the student's ability to solve exercises and answer theoretical questions correctly and consistently. For each correctly completed exercise or theoretical question, 5/30 of the grade will be assigned. The commission reserves the right to conduct an individual interview to define the outcome if the written work is near sufficiency or needs clarification/integration.
